question: In skeletal skeletal muscle of mammals:

options.opa: A motor neuron supplies all its fibers.
options.opb: Each motor neuron supplies a single fiber.
options.opc: Each fiber receives innervation from a single motor neuron.
options.opd: Summation of synaptic potentials is required to reach the excitation threshold.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Motor neuron" -> "innervates multiple muscle fibers" -> "forms a motor unit" -> "opa is correct" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Motor neuron" -> "connects to only one muscle fiber" -> "contradicts typical neuromuscular junction structure" -> "opb is incorrect" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Muscle fiber" -> "receives input from only one motor neuron" -> "prevents conflicting signals" -> "opc is correct" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Neuromuscular junction" -> "single action potential" -> "sufficient to cause muscle fiber contraction" -> "no summation needed for threshold" -> "opd is incorrect" -> 90%
enhanced_information: In skeletal muscle of mammals, each motor neuron innervates multiple muscle fibers, forming a motor unit (Option A correct). Each muscle fiber typically receives input from only one motor neuron, ensuring coordinated function (Option C correct). A single motor neuron does not supply just one fiber (Option B incorrect), and a single action potential is generally sufficient to trigger muscle contraction without needing summation of synaptic potentials (Option D incorrect).
analysis: Option C is supported by the consensus in medical science that each muscle fiber in mammals receives innervation from only one motor neuron. This arrangement ensures efficient and coordinated muscle function, which is a fundamental aspect of muscle physiology.
